docs.title: Week 1 : The Landing Page, and Keeping a Visitor's Trip Idea Alive through Sign-up
The Landing Page and the Draft Across the Sign-up Redirect
Problem
docs.text: The landing page has a small form: destination, dates and budget. A visitor fills it in and presses "Create my itinerary". But only a signed-in user can plan a trip, so the visitor is sent to the sign-up page. Without extra work, the wizard would open empty after sign-up, and everything the visitor typed would be gone.

docs.title: Relevant Context
docs.text:
• The form is trip-planner-widget.tsx.
  • The wizard is trips/new/page.tsx.
  • Between them the visitor goes to the sign-up page, and the page changes more than once, so a normal React state cannot carry the data.

docs.title: Key Observation
docs.text: The data only needs to live for a short time and only in this browser tab. That is what sessionStorage is for. It is cleared when the tab is closed.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
I wrote a small module, lib/draft-storage.ts, with three functions:

saveDraft(draft)   // landing page, just before going to /sign-up
readDraft()        // wizard, to pre-fill its first values
clearDraft()       // wizard, once it has read the draft

Three details made it safe:

  • Every function first checks typeof window === "undefined", because Next.js also runs this code on the server, where there is no window.
  • Every call to sessionStorage is inside try/catch. In some private browsing modes it throws. In that case the draft is simply lost, and the app does not crash.
  • The wizard reads the draft only once, in its first state. It then clears it, so an old draft cannot appear again later.

The landing page form also falls back to safe defaults: "Thailand" if the destination is empty, and 1,50,000 if the budget is not a number.

docs.title: The Rest of the Landing Page
docs.text:
The home page (app/page.tsx) is built from separate sections in components/landing/:

  • Hero has the headline, two buttons ("Start planning" goes to sign-up, "Explore how it works" scrolls down to the four steps) and the planner form described above.
  • HowItWorks explains the flow in four steps: tell us your trip, TripEase plans it, customize everything, travel.
  • ItineraryPreview shows an example trip of 8 days across Bangkok and Phuket. The visitor can press a day number to see that day. The data is a fixed list written in the file, so it is the same for every visitor and is not a generated trip.
  • BudgetPreview shows six example budget bars with fixed amounts.
  • Features has six cards, and FinalCta repeats the sign-up button.
  • The footer says that TripEase is a student project and that prices and names are demo data unless they are linked to a source.

The sections below the hero fade in once, with Framer Motion (whileInView with once: true). A visitor who is already signed in is sent to /dashboard with router.replace, as soon as the sign-in state has finished loading.

docs.title: The Header Inside the App
docs.text: SiteHeader is used by the signed-in pages. It has the logo (a link to the dashboard), a "New trip" button (hidden on small screens), the user's name or email (shown only on large screens) and a "Sign out" button. While signing out, the button is disabled and shows "Signing out…", and afterwards the user is sent to the sign-in page.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: A visitor can type a trip idea, sign up, and arrive in the wizard with the destination, dates and budget already filled in.

docs.title: Week 2 : The Wizard Steps, and a Generation Screen that Shows Only Real Progress
The Wizard Steps, the Wizard Shell and the Generation Loader
Problem
docs.text: Generating a trip takes a few seconds. I wanted the user to see that something is happening, but I did not want a progress bar that moves on a timer or shows a made-up percentage. That would tell the user something that is not true.

docs.title: Relevant Context
docs.text:
The page trips/new/page.tsx has two phases: the wizard and the generating screen. When the user presses "Generate my trip" the page does four things in order:

  1. POST /api/trips/plan decides the cities.
  2. POST /api/trips/generate finds places and builds the itinerary and the budget.
  3. The trip is saved to Firestore.
  4. The browser opens the new roadmap.

docs.title: Key Observation
docs.text: These are the only four real boundaries in the work. "Finding places" and "building the itinerary" look like two steps, but they are one server call. Showing them as two lines would be invented progress, so I did not do it.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
• GenerationLoader has four stages: planning, places, saving and roadmap. A stage moves forward only when the real work moves forward.
  • When the planner returns, the chosen cities are shown straight away under "Your route", with their number of days and the reason. A badge says whether the route was "AI planned" or planned by "TripEase planner" (the fallback). If it is the fallback, a short line says that AI planning was not available.
  • WizardShell shows the six steps (Destination, Dates, Budget, Travelers, Style, Review) as a bar at the top. A step is coloured when it is reached, and the label of the current step is highlighted. The step content slides in with Framer Motion.
  • If anything fails, the page goes back to the wizard and shows the error message, so the user can try again.

docs.title: The Six Steps
docs.text:
The steps are in wizard/steps.tsx. All of them read and write one WizardData object. The budget is kept as text, so the field can be empty while the user types. The update function accepts either a patch or a function of the previous state, so two quick clicks never use an old value.

  • Destination. A text field with focus on load, and six quick choices: Thailand, Bali (Indonesia), Italy, Japan, Goa (India) and Vietnam.
  • Dates. A start date and an end date. The start date is set as the minimum of the end date field.
  • Budget. A currency (INR, USD, EUR or GBP) and an amount. The amount is shown below in large type, formatted with formatMoney, so the user sees immediately what was typed.
  • Travellers. Four types: Solo, Couple, Family and Friends. Choosing one sets a default number of travellers (1, 2, 4 and 4). The plus and minus buttons keep the number between 1 and 20 and change the type to "custom". Both buttons have labels for screen readers.
  • Style. Eight choices (beaches, food, culture, adventure, nightlife, shopping, nature, relaxation). The user can pick as many as they like, and pressing a chosen one removes it.
  • Review. A summary of all values. A missing value shows "—", and an empty style list shows "No preferences selected".

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The user sees the real stages and the real cities, and nothing on the screen claims more than the app has actually done.

docs.title: Week 3 : A Dashboard that Updates Live, the Trip Page and the Roadmap
Dashboard, Trip Page and Roadmap Components
Problem
docs.text: The dashboard has to show the user's own trips, keep the list up to date when a trip changes, and let the user delete a trip without deleting it by accident. The roadmap has to show many small facts about each stop without becoming a wall of text. The trip page has to connect the roadmap, the budget and the map, so that every edit moves all three together.

docs.title: Relevant Context
docs.text: Trips are stored in Firestore. The service subscribeToOwnerTrips calls a function every time the list changes, and returns a function that stops the listening.

docs.title: Solution: Dashboard
docs.text:
• dashboard/page.tsx starts listening when the user is known, and stops listening when the page is left (the cleanup function of useEffect).
  • While the first answer has not come yet, the page shows three grey pulsing cards. trips === null means "not loaded yet", and an empty list means "no trips", so the two cases show different things.
  • Trips are split into "Your trips" and "Past trips" by comparing the end date with today.
  • If the user has no trips, an empty state invites them to create one. If loading fails, an alert shows the error.
  • In TripCard, the bin icon does not delete at once. It changes into "Cancel" and "Confirm" buttons. The card shows the dates, the number of travellers and the budget, formatted with formatMoney.

docs.title: Solution: Roadmap Rows
docs.text:
• CitySection shows the city name and dates, the hotel as a button that opens the hotel editor, and one expandable row for each day. A day row can show a "Transfer" badge, a red warning icon if the day may be too full, and the total cost of the day.
  • ActivityRow uses useSortable from dnd-kit, so a row can be dragged to a new place. The drag handle appears only when the pointer is over the row.
  • Places that do not have a verified source carry a "Demo data" badge, and a stop with no price shows "Free". The reference link opens in a new tab.
  • Clicking a row with a location selects its place on the map.

docs.title: Solution: Trip Page
docs.text:
trips/[tripId]/page.tsx listens to one trip with subscribeToTrip.

  • The page has three cases: while the first answer has not come, a skeleton is shown; if loading fails, an alert shows the error; and if there is no trip, the page says "This trip doesn't exist, or it isn't yours" with a link back to the dashboard.
  • TripHeader shows the title (a pencil icon lets the user rename it, and an empty name is not saved), the dates, the number of nights and cities, and the budget bar. The bar is clamped to 100% and turns red when the estimate is above the budget.
  • There are two tabs, Roadmap and Budget. On a small screen a "Show map" and "Hide map" button controls the map. On a large screen the map stays on the side while the page scrolls.
  • Every edit (add, edit, delete or move an activity, change a hotel, apply a saving) calls a pure function from trip-mutations.ts, which returns the new days or cities together with the recalculated budget. The page then saves them in one write, so the roadmap and the budget cannot disagree.
  • Travel times and warnings are not stored. analyzeTrip runs again after every change, so trips saved earlier are also analysed correctly.
  • The map and the roadmap are linked. Selecting a place on the map opens the day that contains it and scrolls to its row. The map filter follows the day that is open, so the map has no separate day picker.
  • "Edit cities" sends the new city list to /api/trips/rebuild, then saves the cities, days, budget and planning record in one write, and clears the selection so it cannot point at a removed city.

docs.title: Solution: Day View
docs.text:
• The header shows "Day N · City", the date, a line such as "~6.5h planned · 1.5h travel (est.)" and the planned cost of the day.
  • Activities are sortable. The drag starts only after the pointer moves 4 pixels, so a normal click on a row is not taken as a drag. After a drop the new order is passed up and the travel rows are calculated again.
  • A city transfer is shown at the top of the day as a dashed card, for example "Bangkok → Phuket" with the mode, the time and the distance, and it says "estimated". It is not shown as an activity, because getting to a city is not something to do there. The legs between stops are small grey lines marked "(est.)".
  • FeasibilityNotes shows each note by its level: a red note for a problem, an amber one for a warning and plain grey text for information. Nothing blocks the user. The notes only say what the engine noticed.
  • An empty day shows "No activities yet — add the first one."

docs.title: Solution: Editing Dialogs
docs.text:
• Hotel dialog. The user can change the name, the price per night and the nights. The price cannot go below 0 and the nights cannot go below 1. If the name is changed, the hotel is marked as demo data and its link, rating, image and source are removed, because it is no longer the place that was found. If only the price or nights change, the source stays, and the price is marked as exact because the user typed it.
  • Activity dialog. Adding and editing use the same dialog. The name is required, and a reference link must be a full URL. A hand-typed activity is marked as demo data. If an existing activity is renamed, it is marked as demo data again and its rating, image, source and location are removed, and the old link is dropped unless the user changed it.
  • Place search. Inside the activity dialog, a search box calls /api/places/search with the user's sign-in token. It needs at least two characters, also works with the Enter key and shows a spinner. Each result shows the name, a "Demo" badge if needed, the rating, the address, the coordinates and an estimated price. Picking one fills the name, category, description, duration, cost and link, and keeps its location and source. If the user types over the name afterwards, the picked place is detached. If the search fails, a message says that the user can still type a name.
  • City dialog. Each row has a city name and its days. Adding or removing a city shares the days again with splitDaysAcrossCities, keeping the relative sizes. "Add city" is disabled when there are as many cities as days, and a single remaining city cannot be removed. A counter shows "X of N days allocated", in green when it is correct and in amber when it is not. The dialog uses validateCityAllocation, the same check that the AI planner's result must pass, and "Save cities" stays disabled until it passes. The first problem is shown as a warning, and an error from the server is shown below it.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The dashboard is always in step with the data, deleting needs two clicks, every roadmap row shows where its information came from, and an edit changes the roadmap, the budget and the map together.

docs.title: Week 4 : The Budget Panel, the Map and the Validation Schemas
Budget Panel, Map and Zod Schemas
Budget panel
docs.text:
Problem. The budget has a lot of numbers: total, estimate, eight categories and the savings suggestions. They have to be read at a glance.

What I did. BudgetPanel compares the estimate with the budget:

  • The difference is shown as "remaining" or "over", and a bar shows the percentage. The bar is clamped to 100% and turns red when the trip is over budget.
  • A warning alert appears when the estimate is above the budget, and a success alert when it is not.
  • A Recharts bar chart shows the spending by category (categories with zero are left out), and a list below shows every category with its amount.
  • If there are savings suggestions, each one has a title, a description, the saving and an "Apply" button.

docs.title: Map card
docs.text:
Problem. Leaflet needs window when it is imported. On the server there is no window, so the page would fail.

What I did. TripMap loads the Leaflet layer with dynamic(..., { ssr: false }) and shows "Loading map…" meanwhile. The map points are built from the live trip, never from a separate fixed list, so the map always matches what the traveller edited. If a selected point is filtered out, the selection is cleared, so no row stays highlighted without a marker.

PlaceCard shows only what the trip really has. A place with no rating shows no rating, and a place with no real reference link shows no link. "Free" is shown only when the cost is recorded as zero.

docs.title: Map layer
docs.text:
leaflet-map.tsx is the part that draws the map.

  • Tiles. The map uses OpenStreetMap tiles, which need no key, so the map also works in demo mode. In dark mode the tiles are slightly dimmed with CSS, and the markers and cards keep their own colours.
  • Markers. I used my own round markers instead of Leaflet's default pins. A stop shows its number in the day, a hotel shows a hotel emoji, and the colour tells the type: orange for sights, red for food and indigo for hotels. The selected marker is larger.
  • Keyboard and screen readers. Each marker is given the role of a button, a name such as "Wat Pho — day 1, Bangkok" and a pressed state. Enter selects it, and I added the Space key too, as a button would normally allow.
  • Scrolling. A plain mouse wheel scrolls the page, so the map does not trap the reader. For one and a half seconds a hint says "Use Ctrl + scroll to zoom the map". With Ctrl (or Cmd) the wheel zooms the map around the cursor.
  • Viewport. The map fits all visible points with a margin and a maximum zoom of 14. It fits again when its container changes size, because on a small screen the map can be created while it is still hidden and has no size. Selecting a point centres it without animation.
  • Lines. An orange dashed line follows the order of the day. A blue dotted line joins the cities. Neither is a driving route, and no routing service is used.

Two test files check these components: leaflet-map.test.tsx (the wheel behaviour and the marker names, states and keys) and place-card.test.tsx (what the card shows, and what it must not invent).

docs.title: Validation schemas and demo data
docs.text:
Problem. A wrong value from the AI or from a user must not reach a saved trip.

What I did. lib/validation/trip.ts has Zod schemas that mirror the types. For example, the destination must have 2 to 80 characters, the budget must be positive and at most 100,000,000, there can be 1 to 20 travellers, and the currency is one of INR, USD, EUR or GBP. The itinerary produced by the generator is checked against generatedItinerarySchema before it is returned, so a bad result fails in the API route instead of being saved.

lib/mock-data/fx.ts holds fixed, approximate conversion rates, so the demo generator can show amounts in the currency the user picked. They are not live rates, and the file says so.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The budget, the map and the saved data all show only values that are checked, and say clearly when a value is only an estimate.
